provenance.instrument: Township of South Hanover Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. No. 2-1995 of 4-11-1995, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 SO2457, Township of South Hanover, PA. 27-1401 names 'the Township of South Hanover Dauphin County, Pennsylvania', and the township website (southhanover.org, Code of Ordinances) links its code to eCode360, so this is South Hanover township, Dauphin County. Every district's uses and figures are text in Chapter 27. The one attachment is a sign table. New Laws: none listed
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 shows 'Includes legislation through 10-10-2023'. New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code'
provenance.code_caution: The online code includes legislation only through 10-10-2023, and the Township's own page warns that amendments may have been enacted since. The Township page posts a Draft Data Center Ordinance for advertisement, a Data Center Toolkit and a Data Center Overlay Map. News reports say the supervisors voted to advertise a data center overlay ordinance with its own overlay map and set a vote for March 24, 2026. Whether it was adopted, and which residential land the overlay covers, was not confirmed. Ask the Township office for the zoning text in force before relying on these rules
checks: Accessory apartment: a conditional use in R-A, ESC, R-S, R-U and R-C (in R-C 'when associated with a single-family detached dwelling'), decided by the Board of Supervisors after public notice and hearing and Planning Commission review (27-403.3, 27-4A03.1, 27-503.1, 27-603.1, 27-1003.4, 27-2109). It is created inside a single-family detached dwelling, 'incorporated within an existing single-family detached dwelling without any substantial external modification' (27-1502.15, 27-203 'Apartment, accessory')

The apartment is one complete and separate housekeeping unit 'to be used/occupied by a person or persons related by marriage or blood relative only'. The owner lives in one of the units except for bona fide temporary absences. The building keeps the look of a single-family detached dwelling. At most 30% of the structure's total floor area and not over 400 sq ft, at least 300 sq ft. At least three off-street spaces in all for owner and tenant (27-1502.15). 27-1509 also sets 300 sq ft for 'conversion/accessory apartments', but 150 sq ft for apartments 'designed for and occupied extensively by one person'

Guesthouse (a dwelling unit for visitors, attached or detached, 'not ... offered for occupancy for compensation', Ord. No. 5-2021) and domestic employee quarters (for maids, butlers, cooks and the like of the household, attached or detached) are conditional uses in R-A, ESC, R-S, R-U, R-M, V and R-C. 27-1502.27 allows them 'on a lot in any residential district' as accessory uses to a single-family detached dwelling: two acres when detached, more if needed for on-lot sewage or water, handled as a land development with a land development plan, and a recorded covenant that they are never subdivided off (27-203, 27-1502.27). A guesthouse or quarters is a dwelling unit, so it needs at least 600 sq ft of habitable floor area (27-1509), and in R-A, R-S and R-C, where density is one dwelling unit per acre, a lot with one may need two acres even when it is attached to the house (27-405, 27-505, 27-1005.1A). A detached guesthouse on two acres may be 19 ft tall if it stands at least 25 ft from every side and rear lot line, and taller by one foot for each added foot of that distance, up to 35 ft. Closer than 25 ft it is at most 14 ft (27-1506.4)

Country estates (conditional use in R-A, lots of five acres or more) may hold 'an accessory apartment, guesthouse or servants quarters which shall be considered accessory uses' but no second principal dwelling (27-1502.29G)

Two-family dwellings: R-M permits 'Two-family detached (duplex dwellings)', one unit over the other, with both public sewer and water, 7,000 sq ft per unit, 80 ft wide, front 25 ft, side 10 ft, rear 25 ft, 30% coverage (27-702.1E, 27-705.1C, 27-203). V permits 'single- and two-family' residential uses: two-family detached 7,200 sq ft per unit and 50 ft wide, two-family semi-detached 4,500 sq ft per unit and 60 ft wide, 30% coverage, both with public sewer and water (27-802.1A, 27-805.1A). Two spaces per dwelling, plus one for each additional bedroom in a dwelling with four or more bedrooms, and for a residential property a space in a garage does not count (27-1802). V also permits apartments and multifamily dwellings, a path for three or more units

Coverage in every district is 'Total coverage', the building area and impervious material together (27-203 'Coverage'). Since Ord. No. 1-2018 decks, parking and driveway areas that do not prevent infiltration are not counted as impervious, and gravel or crushed stone is assumed impervious unless designed as an infiltration practice (27-203 'Coverage' 2). Accessory buildings are at most 14 ft tall in every residential district, may stand only in one side yard or the rear yard, at least 5 ft from the side or rear line and 10 ft from the house (5 ft with no windows in facing walls), 20 ft from an alley center line, and never in a front yard (27-404, 27-504, 27-604, 27-704, 27-804, 27-1004, 27-1508.1C(3), D(4)). On a corner lot in a residential district an accessory building may not stand within 30 ft of the exterior side lot line, and on the side street it keeps the front yard depth (27-1508.1D(4)(g), (h)). On a lot of two acres or more an accessory building at least 25 ft from every side and rear lot line may be 19 ft tall, and one more foot for each added foot of that distance, up to 35 ft (27-1506.4). A residential building may rise above 35 ft by one foot for each added foot of every yard, up to 40 ft (27-1506.1). A lot without both public water and public sewer needs one acre and 100 ft of width (27-1507.1). No dwelling unit under 600 sq ft (27-1509)

Floodplain District: 27-301 lists FP among the zoning districts, and its boundaries are those of the Flood Insurance Study, not the zoning map (27-302). It covers Zones AE and A1-30 on the FIRM of 8-2-2012 (27-1403.1, 27-1408.1). Its use list has agriculture, floodproofed residential dwellings, yards, recreation, storage, small accessory buildings and utilities, and no accessory apartment, guesthouse or domestic employee quarters (27-1403.2.1). Its own figures: one acre of lot area and of lot area per dwelling unit, 150 ft wide, front 50 ft, two side yards of 30 ft, rear 30 ft, total coverage 30% with half the lot vegetated, 35 ft (27-1403.3 to 27-1403.7). Whether the base district's conditional uses still apply inside it is not settled. Zone A areas are identified floodplain under Article XIV without being in the FP District. An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', is at most 100 sq ft and has no sanitary facilities (27-1409.2.4). In special and approximate floodplain areas no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank (27-1408.2.1B(2)(a), C(2)(a)). In a floodway no encroachment that would raise flood heights, and no new construction without a DEP permit (27-1408.2.1A). Without a designated floodway, no new development unless all past and projected development raises the base flood elevation by at most one foot (27-1408.2.1B(2)(b)). New construction or a substantial improvement of a residence has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (27-1409.2.1). A fully enclosed space below the lowest floor is only for parking, access or storage, with flood openings (27-1409.2.3). An on-site sewage system goes in the floodplain only in strict compliance with state and local rules (27-1409.3.1C(3)). Manufactured homes are barred in a floodway and within 50 ft of the top of bank (27-1409.6). Work of 50% or more of market value fully complies (27-1411.2). No variance for anything in a floodway that raises the base flood elevation (27-1412.2.2). Applications go to the County Conservation District for review (27-1407.5)

Lots of record: on an unimproved lot held in single and separate ownership when the chapter took effect, below the district's lot area or width, a building may be put up if the yards are met and the sewage system is approved (27-1507.2). On a lot of record below the district width only one single-family dwelling may be erected (27-1508.1D(2)). A permit for any construction or earth moving first needs an erosion and sedimentation control plan and a surface water management plan approved by the Township Engineer (27-1513.1), and an on-lot sewage system needs a state adequacy statement before a building permit (27-1511.1)

R-C cluster option (conditional use, a tract of at least 50 acres with public sewer and water): 'Each dwelling unit shall be located on its own individual lot. All units/lots shall be for sale only.' Detached lots are at least 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft wide, with front 25 ft, sides 10 ft each and rear 25 ft (27-1010.1). So whether an accessory apartment may be added on a cluster lot is not settled

A use 'neither specifically permitted or denied' is referred to the Zoning Hearing Board, which may permit it if it is 'similar to and compatible with permitted uses in the district' (27-1505). Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 27-2112.1C, which follow MPC 910.2. No bar on a use variance was found

The online code includes legislation only through 10-10-2023. The Township's Code of Ordinances page says amendments may be enacted after the last revision of the electronic code, and posts a draft Data Center Ordinance for advertisement. Ask the Township office whether any zoning ordinance adopted since then changes these rules
provenance.notes: Zoning office: South Hanover Township Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-18. Read: Articles IV, IVA, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X and XIII in full, Article XI by page search for dwellings, Article XIV (Floodplain District) in full, Article XV 27-1501 to 27-1503, 27-1505, 27-1507 to 27-1509, the 27-1802 parking table, 27-2108, 27-2109 and 27-2112, and the 27-203 definitions of accessory apartment, coverage, domestic employees quarters, dwelling types, dwelling unit and guesthouse (by screenshots). Also read from the saved text: Article XII (OP), Article XVI (nonconforming), 27-301, 27-302, 27-1504 to 27-1516 and the 27-203 coverage definition. Not read: Articles XIVA, XIVB, XVII, XIX and XX, the rest of 27-203 (family, new construction and regulatory flood elevation among them), a short-term rental article (Ord. No. 7-2018), the zoning map, and the draft Data Center Ordinance, toolkit and overlay map (documents, not opened). Saved text in the batch 53 cache.

ESC permits only 'Dwellings and student homes for employees and students of eleemosynary schools' (27-4A02.2) on 50 acres, and the apartment goes inside a single-family detached dwelling, so in ESC it reaches only such a school dwelling

value.name: Guesthouse or domestic employee quarters inside or attached to the house
value.conditions: A guesthouse (a dwelling unit for visitors, never offered for occupancy for compensation) or domestic employee quarters (for domestic employees of the household), as an accessory use to a single-family detached dwelling. Handled as a land development, with a land development plan, and a recorded covenant that it is never subdivided off. All other district standards apply. No lot minimum beyond the district's for a unit attached to the house in 27-1502.27. The unit needs at least 600 sq ft of habitable floor area (27-1509)

requires.condition: Occupied by visitors, never for compensation (guesthouse), or by domestic employees of the household (domestic employee quarters)

disputed_districts.note: 27-1502.27 allows a guesthouse or domestic employee quarters 'on a lot in any residential district', while R-MH lists no conditional uses and permits only mobile homes in a park

value.note: A guesthouse may not be rented out, so it is not a rental unit

disputed_min_lot.note: Density there is one dwelling unit per acre, and a guesthouse or quarters is a dwelling unit, so a lot with the house and one may need two acres

value.name: Detached guesthouse or domestic employee quarters (two acres)
value.conditions: A guesthouse (a dwelling unit for visitors, never offered for occupancy for compensation) or domestic employee quarters (for domestic employees of the household), as an accessory use to a single-family detached dwelling. Handled as a land development, with a land development plan, and a recorded covenant that it is never subdivided off. All other district standards apply. A detached unit needs a lot of at least two acres, more if needed for on-lot sewage or water, and at least 600 sq ft of habitable floor area (27-1509). In a side or rear yard. On two acres the accessory building may be 19 ft tall if it stands at least 25 ft from every side and rear lot line, and taller by one foot for each added foot of that distance, up to 35 ft. Closer than 25 ft it is at most 14 ft (27-1506.4)

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (duplex) (R-M)
value.conditions: A building for two families, one unit over the other, with two side yards. Both public sewer and public water. 7,000 sq ft of lot per unit, 80 ft wide, front 25 ft, side 10 ft, rear 25 ft, coverage 30%. Two parking spaces per dwelling
value.note: 14,000 sq ft is two units at 7,000. Whether reworking an existing house into one unit over another counts as a duplex is not settled

value.name: Two-family dwelling (V)
value.conditions: 'single- and two-family' residential uses. With both public sewer and water: two-family detached 7,200 sq ft of lot per unit and 50 ft wide, two-family semi-detached 4,500 sq ft per unit and 60 ft wide, coverage 30%. Front 20 ft, sides 5 ft, rear 20 ft. Two parking spaces per dwelling
value.note: 14,400 sq ft is two units of a two-family detached dwelling at 7,200. A two-family semi-detached building needs 9,000 sq ft. Whether adding a unit to an existing house makes a two-family dwelling is not settled

building_types.note: Only in a single-family detached dwelling

existing_structure_only.note: 'incorporated within an existing single-family detached dwelling without any substantial external modification'

historic_bypass.note: The zoning chapter has no historic path

districts_read_no_listing.note: No accessory apartment. R-M and V list guesthouses and domestic employee quarters and permit two-family dwellings. R-MH permits only mobile homes in a park. IP lists no dwelling (read by page search). OP lists offices, clinics, schools and the like, no dwelling (27-1202). CH allows only its listed uses, with transient lodging and no dwelling (27-1302.1)

value.condition: One apartment in a single-family detached dwelling, 'to be used/occupied by a person or persons related by marriage or blood relative only', with the owner living in one of the units.

The apartment is a complete and separate housekeeping unit that can be isolated from the original unit, made without any substantial external modification, and the building keeps, as far as feasible, the look of a single-family detached dwelling.
Floodplain District: an accessory structure 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', is at most 100 sq ft and has no sanitary facilities.
Floodplain District: in special and approximate floodplain areas no new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse.

Floodplain District: residential dwellings are floodproofed per the building code, and new construction or a substantial improvement of a residence has its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. Work of 50% or more of market value fully complies, smaller work is elevated or floodproofed as far as possible. No expansion in a floodway that raises the base flood elevation, and no variance for it.

Floodplain District: the code makes FP a zoning district of its own (27-301), drawn from the Flood Insurance Study (27-302). Its use list has agriculture, floodproofed residential dwellings, yards, recreation, storage, small accessory buildings and utilities, and no accessory apartment, guesthouse or domestic employee quarters, and it lists no conditional uses. Its own figures: one acre of lot area and of lot area per dwelling unit, 150 ft wide, front 50 ft, two side yards of 30 ft, rear 30 ft, total coverage at most 30% with half the lot vegetated, height 35 ft. The FP District covers only Zones AE and A1-30.

disputed_by.note: The FP District is drawn from the Flood Insurance Study, while the base districts stay on the zoning map beneath it, and Article XIV supersedes other provisions only where they conflict. Whether the base district's conditional uses, the accessory apartment among them, still apply inside the FP District is not settled

value.condition: R-C cluster development: each dwelling unit is on its own individual lot, and all units and lots are for sale only. An accessory apartment would put a second dwelling unit on a cluster lot, so whether it may be added there is not settled. Cluster lots are at least 10,000 sq ft and 80 ft wide, with front 25 ft, sides 10 ft each and rear 25 ft.
